classes.a2a-abuse: Require authentication on every A2A operation, scope tasks and push configurations to the caller that created them, return 404 for tasks the caller may not see, and reject push callback URLs that point at loopback, private or link-local addresses.
classes.credential-extraction: Keep keys, tokens, passwords and wallet seeds out of the model's context: load them inside the tool layer, never in a prompt. Scan replies for secret patterns and redact them before they leave the agent.
classes.data-exfil: Allowlist the domains, email addresses and tools the agent may send data to, and block the rest in code. Strip sensitive fields from tool results before the model sees them, and log every outbound send.
classes.excessive-agency: Ask the user to confirm irreversible or high-impact actions such as deleting data, sending messages, installing packages or calling cloud APIs. Run the agent with least-privilege credentials so one wrong decision cannot do much damage.
classes.harmful-content: Filter input and output for the harm categories your use case forbids, and test the filter with reworded and multi-turn requests.
classes.indirect-injection: Mark web pages, files, emails and tool results as untrusted content that cannot give orders. Only the user's own request may authorize a tool call, so ask the user before acting on anything that fetched content asks for.
classes.input-handling: Check the size, type and encoding of every input before the model sees it. Decode or reject base64, hidden Unicode characters and unexpected file types instead of passing them through.
classes.jailbreak: Filter both input and output for the content your policy forbids, whatever the role-play, encoding or framing. Check the whole conversation, not only the last message, so a request split over several turns is still refused.
classes.mcp-abuse: Connect only to MCP servers you have approved, and pin each tool's name and description. Stop the session when a server changes a tool mid-session, ignore instructions inside tool descriptions and results, and call only the tools the user's task needs.
classes.misinformation: Ground answers in sources the agent can cite, and have it say it does not know when the sources do not support an answer. Show the citations so users can check each claim.
classes.output-handling: Treat model output as untrusted input to the next system. Escape it before you render HTML, use parameterized queries, and never pass it to a shell, eval or interpreter without a strict allowlist.
classes.payment-abuse: Enforce spending rules in code, outside the model: a budget per payment and per task, a payee allowlist, and a check that the amount and payee match what the user approved. Ask the user before paying more than the limit or paying a new payee, and cap the total across retries.
classes.poisoning: Check the source and integrity of content before it enters a retrieval index, agent memory or training data. Record where each entry came from so you can find and remove poisoned content.
classes.prompt-injection: A user message can ask for things but cannot change the system prompt's rules or the agent's tool permissions. Keep both fixed for the whole session, and enforce high-impact limits in code instead of relying on the model to refuse.
classes.resource-abuse: Set hard limits per task on tool calls, loop iterations, tokens, time and spend, and stop the task when it reaches one. Alert on runs that come close to a limit.
classes.supply-chain: Pin and verify every package, model, plugin and MCP server the agent installs or loads. Block install scripts and new dependencies until a person approves them.
classes.tool-abuse: Give each tool the narrowest scope it needs and validate every argument in code against an allowlist. Ask the user to confirm any tool call that writes, deletes, sends or spends.

probes.mcp_scan_command_execution: Never build a shell command from tool input. Call the program directly with an argument list, check each argument against an allowlist, and run the tool with the least privilege it needs.
probes.mcp_scan_cross_session_leak: Keep each session's state separate on the server. Key stored values by session or user, clear them when the session ends, and never return one client's data to another.
probes.mcp_scan_description_instructions: Write tool names and descriptions for the user, not as orders to the model. Remove text that tells the model what to do or what to hide from the user, and review metadata changes like code changes.
probes.mcp_scan_hidden_characters: Strip zero-width, bidirectional and other invisible Unicode characters from tool metadata and results before you return them, so the text a person reviews is the text the model reads.
probes.mcp_scan_input_reflection: Do not echo tool input back verbatim. Return structured fields, or mark echoed text as data, so an attacker's input cannot come back to the model as an instruction.
probes.mcp_scan_path_traversal: Resolve every path argument to an absolute path and refuse it unless it stays inside the tool's root directory. Reject parent-directory steps, absolute paths and symlinks that lead outside the root.
probes.mcp_scan_readonly_tool_wrote: Set the read-only annotation only on tools that cannot write. Run those tools with a read-only filesystem or read-only credentials, or remove the annotation.
probes.mcp_scan_result_injection: Treat content your tools fetch as data. Return it in a field marked as untrusted, and strip or flag text in it that gives the model instructions before you send the result.
probes.mcp_scan_schema_instructions: Keep input schema descriptions to what each parameter means and which values it accepts. Remove text that tells the model what to do, and review schema changes like code changes.
probes.mcp_scan_secret_in_result: Never return credentials, tokens or keys in tool results. Redact secret-shaped values on the server before you send a result, and keep secrets out of the data the tool can read.
probes.mcp_scan_tool_list_changed: Keep the tool list stable within a session: never add, remove or change a tool's name, description, schema or behavior after a client has listed it. Ship tool changes as a new server version that clients review again.
probes.mcp_server_foreign_origin: Reject requests whose Origin header is not one you trust, and send no permissive CORS headers. Bind a local server to 127.0.0.1 and check the Host header so a web page cannot reach it through DNS rebinding.
probes.mcp_server_known_vulnerable_version: Upgrade the MCP server to a release that fixes the advisory named in the finding. Until then, keep it off untrusted networks and require authentication.
probes.mcp_server_no_auth: Require authentication on the MCP endpoint, such as a bearer token or OAuth, and refuse initialize without valid credentials.
probes.mcp_server_sensitive_tools: Remove tools that dump environment variables, run arbitrary commands or read arbitrary files. If a tool must stay, limit it to named values or one directory, and require authentication.
